# Self-improvement log

## Replace Docker Compose with kind + Terraform

- Step 1 (2026-10-12): first `npm run start:dev` took ~19 minutes, almost all of it `npm ci` inside the first image builds, and overran the 10 minute foreground limit. Added a note to `PROCESS.md` step 6 to expect this and to poll with an `until pgrep` loop instead of `sleep`. Also recorded that infra steps are verified by really running `start:dev` twice and `stop:dev` twice (idempotence) plus `terraform test` per module.
- Step 2 (2026-10-12): a pinned third-party image tag I wrote from memory (`minio/mc`) did not exist and only failed at `kind load`, minutes into `start:dev`. Added a note to `PROCESS.md` to check new image tags with `docker manifest inspect` (or an image already on the host) before the first run.
- Step 3 (2026-10-12): the ZITADEL image is distroless (no `cat`), so reading the PAT out of the running pod failed silently with an empty value; use a throwaway busybox pod that mounts the claim instead. Also, ingress rules like `!PathPrefix(...)` cannot be written as plain Kubernetes Ingress, which is why Traefik uses its file provider here. No process change; both are specific to this feature.
- Step 4 (2026-10-13): nothing new went wrong; image tags were checked first and the cold-run cost was already paid, so the run took minutes. A real trace posted to `localhost:8080/v1/traces` and read back from `localhost:8080/jaeger/api/traces/<id>` is a cheap scripted check that replaces opening the UI. No process change.
- Step 5 (2026-10-13): two cluster-only bugs that `terraform test` cannot see. A Service named like a component injects `<NAME>_PORT=tcp://...` into every pod in the namespace and broke images that read their own `<NAME>_PORT` (Ollama, Qwen-TTS), so those pods set `enable_service_links = false`. Beatrice does not reconnect when RabbitMQ is down at startup, and Terraform's rollout wait only helps if the dependency is declared. Both only showed in pod logs, so for infra steps a pod being `Running` is not proof: read the app's own log or query the dependency (here `rabbitmqctl list_queues` showing a consumer). Terraform also panicked mid-apply while a deployment was failing its rollout, losing state; recovery was `kind delete cluster` plus removing the state files. No process change.
- Step 6 (2026-10-13): the codegen Job first ran as the host user (so generated files are not root-owned) and failed because `prisma generate` writes into the image's root-owned `node_modules`; running as root and `chown`-ing the mounted sources afterwards fixed it. A failed Job's pod is deleted with it, so its logs were gone; reproducing the exact container in a one-off `kubectl apply` pod is the quick way to see why. Also a Service named `backend` or `frontend` injects `BACKEND_PORT=tcp://...` and would shadow `.env`; pods that read `*_PORT` need `enable_service_links = false`. No process change.
- Step 6 (2026-10-13, after review): I first put hot reload (`dev_source_path`, `hostPath`, a start-script ConfigMap, dev-only Jobs) inside `modules/backend` and `modules/frontend`, against the requirement that modules are identical locally and in AWS. Moved all of it to `envs/local` behind generic inputs (`volumes`, `command`, `files`, `pre_deploy_jobs`). Added a grep check to `PROCESS.md`. Also: module-level `depends_on` on a module whose `routes` output feeds the ingress closes a dependency cycle; order through an input value instead.
- Step 7 (2026-10-13): adding kind port mappings changes the cluster definition, which Terraform wants to replace; `stop:dev` then failed refreshing resources on a cluster whose provider was unknown, leaving a running cluster and stale state. `stop:dev` now falls back to `kind delete cluster` plus dropping the state, since the environment is throwaway. Lesson for any later step that edits `kind_cluster`: run `stop:dev` on the old definition before changing it. Unlike the other steps, devtools images were pinned to concrete tags (checked with `docker manifest inspect`) instead of the floating `main` and `latest` from compose.
